title: Best checking accounts with no fees
summary: Compare the best checking accounts with no fees, including our pick and other options, plus how to choose the account that fits how you bank.
body_markdown:
A true no-fee checking account has no monthly maintenance fee, no minimum balance requirement, and free ATM access. There are no hoops (like a required balance or direct deposit) just to keep the account free.


-


**Axos Checking** meets all three with no monthly maintenance fees, no minimums, no overdraft fees, and 1.00% APY with qualifying direct deposit.


-


**Other options** include a mix of online and big-bank accounts like Capital One 360, Ally, Discover, and Charles Schwab.


-


**How to choose** comes down to factors like ATM access, overdraft policies, deposit options, and interest.


[Summarize with ChatGPT](https://chatgpt.com/?q=Summarize+this+article%3A+https%3A%2F%2Fwww.axosbank.com%2Fpersonal%2Finsights%2Ffinance%2Fdigital-banking%2Fbest-checking-accounts-with-no-fees)


### Axos Checking


[Axos Checking](https://www.axosbank.com/personal/bank/checking-accounts/axos-checking?utm_content=insights) covers all three requirements and then some. There's no monthly maintenance fee, no minimum balance requirement, no overdraft fees, and no fee to open the account.


You get access to more than 95,000 fee-free ATMs nationwide, plus unlimited reimbursement for domestic out-of-network ATM fees, so you can withdraw cash almost anywhere without paying for it.


The account can also earn interest. Set up qualifying direct deposits of at least $1 per month and your balance earns 1.00% APY for that statement cycle.


Direct deposit customers can access their paycheck up to two days early as well.


**Best for:** Anyone who wants a genuinely free everyday account that also pays interest with minimal requirements.


### Capital One 360 Checking


Capital One 360 Checking is a solid pick if you want a no-fee account from a big bank with physical locations.


There's no monthly fee or minimum balance, and Capital One has eliminated overdraft fees. You also get access to a large fee-free ATM network.


The tradeoff: it doesn't reimburse fees charged by out-of-network ATMs, so you'll want to stay inside the network.


### Ally Bank Spending Account


Ally is an online-only bank known for customer-friendly policies. Its checking account has no monthly fee, no minimum balance, and no overdraft fees.


Ally also offers a large fee-free ATM network plus a monthly allowance of reimbursement for out-of-network ATM fees.


Ally's app includes budgeting tools like spending "buckets" that let you organize money for different goals inside one account.


### Discover Cashback Debit


Discover's checking account charges no monthly fee and no fees for insufficient funds, and it offers something unusual: cash back on debit card purchases, up to a monthly cap. It also connects to a large fee-free ATM network.


The catch is that Discover doesn't reimburse out-of-network ATM fees, and it's online-only, so there are no branches.


### Charles Schwab Investor Checking


Schwab's checking account is a favorite among travelers. It has no monthly fee, no minimums, and unlimited ATM fee rebates worldwide, which makes it one of the few accounts that stays free even when you're withdrawing cash abroad. It also links to a Schwab brokerage account.


The account earns minimal interest, so it works best as a spending account rather than a place to park cash.


No monthly fee is the baseline, not the finish line. Here's how to compare beyond that:


-


**Match the account to your habits:** If you withdraw cash often, prioritize ATM reimbursement. If you rarely touch cash, interest or cash back may matter more.


-


**Check the overdraft policy:** Many online banks have dropped overdraft fees entirely. If an account still charges one, find out how much and whether you can opt out.


-


**Look at deposit options:** Online banks make cash deposits harder. If you handle cash regularly, confirm how (and whether) you can deposit it for free.


-


**Confirm FDIC insurance:** Every account on this list is FDIC insured up to $250,000 per depositor, per bank. If you're using a fintech app rather than a bank, verify which partner bank holds your money.


-


**Read the full fee schedule:** "No monthly fee" doesn't always mean no fees at all. Scan for charges on wire transfers, paper statements, or expedited debit card replacement.


The best checking accounts with no fees remove the monthly maintenance charge, skip balance requirements, and keep ATM access free.


Online banks like Axos, Ally, and Discover lead the category, while Capital One and Schwab offer strong no-fee options with their own perks.


The right choice comes down to how you bank: cash access, interest, cash back, or travel flexibility.


Whichever account you pick, the goal is the same: **your checking account should hold your money, not take it.**
